newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union head calls for new talks on growth.
newsitem.headline: German union head calls for new talks on growth.

text.p: The head of Germany's white collar workers union DAG said the Bundesbank and opposition Social Democrats must be invited to participate in top-level talks aimed at finding ways to boost economic growth.

DAG head Roland Issen told the newspaper Berliner Zeitung that he would favour restarting a series of meetings between government leaders, unions and employers to try to solve some of Germany's pressing problems, like unemployment.
"But a meeting like this would be useless without the SPD and the Bundesbank," Issen said in a summary of an article to be published on Monday.

The SPD must be included as it commands a majority in Bonn's upper house, the Bundesrat, and the Bundesbank must be included because it is instrumental in setting the tone for investments in Germany, Issen said.
The Bonn government last year held several of these meetings, but they ended without achieving much.
Issen also criticised the government for having its sights set too firmly on joining Europe's planned currency union in 1999.
"The price for the euro cannot be ever rising unemployment rates," Issen said . On Thursday Germany reported 4.66 million people were unemployed in January, the largest number since 1933.
